facts.text: A request for proposal (RFP) asks vendors for a solution and price; a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) enables confidential information sharing; a statement of work specifies supplier deliverables; and supplier information provides technical data needed to simulate a sensor or tool vendor's product.
facts.quote: A request for proposal (RFP) asks vendors to propose a solution and a price, a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) lets two companies share secrets safely, a statement of work spells out exactly what a supplier will deliver

facts.text: For this program, simulation-tool RFPs should price peak concurrent workers, continuous-integration and cloud rights, subcontractor access, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) nodes and disaster-recovery environments, rather than only desktop seats.
facts.quote: the RFP should price peak concurrent workers, continuous-integration and cloud rights, subcontractor access, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) nodes and disaster-recovery environments, not only desktop seats

facts.text: Simulation-tool RFPs should require export in open formats: ASAM Open Simulation Interface (OSI), OpenSCENARIO, Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) and OpenUSD.

facts.text: Two large simulation vendors changed ownership during 2025 and 2026.

facts.text: An engineering partner's statement of work should require editable machine models, scene and source assets, parameter provenance, correlation datasets, test definitions, continuous-integration scripts, version manifests, known-limitation registers and interface specifications, rather than only test reports.
facts.quote: editable machine models, scene and source assets, parameter provenance, correlation datasets, test definitions, continuous-integration (CI) scripts, version manifests, known-limitation registers and interface specifications, not only test reports

facts.text: A credible lidar simulation model needs supplier information on scan pattern, beam divergence, wavelength, transmit power, detector model, detection thresholds and the signal-processing chain.
facts.quote: For lidar: scan pattern, beam divergence, wavelength, transmit power, detector model, detection thresholds and the signal-processing chain.

facts.text: A credible radar simulation model needs supplier information on carrier band, waveform, antenna patterns, receiver noise, detection and tracking logic, and radome properties.
facts.quote: For radar: carrier band, waveform, antenna patterns, receiver noise, detection and tracking logic, radome properties.

facts.text: A credible camera simulation model needs supplier information on lens distortion, spectral response, shutter timing, noise, exposure control and the image-processing pipeline.
facts.quote: For cameras: lens distortion, spectral response, shutter timing, noise, exposure control and the image-processing pipeline.

facts.text: Credible models of all sensors need exact mounting pose and tolerances, the machine's vibration transfer function, firmware version and degradation modes.
facts.quote: For all sensors: exact mounting pose and tolerances, the machine's vibration transfer function, firmware version and degradation modes.

facts.text: If a sensor supplier refuses to share internals, five options remain: request a black-box model packaged to OSI as a Functional Mock-up Unit (FMU), characterize the sensor in controlled tests, estimate parameters inversely from measurements, put the real sensor in the loop, or add model-delivery and validation-data requirements to the sourcing contract while sensor choice remains open.
facts.quote: ask for a black-box model packaged to OSI as a Functional Mock-up Unit (FMU), characterize the sensor yourself in controlled tests, estimate parameters inversely from measurements, put the real sensor in the loop
